title: The Theosis Framework
prompts: What would a deliberate 24-hour rhythm look like if your evening made room for stillness and prepared you for the next morning?
How can sleep, food, movement, and prayer support one another in your actual week?
Recall a season when your old way of living stopped working. What did it teach you about what was underneath the habit?
What enduring truth about God and the soul can anchor your daily attention? Whose example helps you remember it?
What needs to change in the next forty days, and what concrete fruit would you look for by day ninety?
What story do you tell yourself just before compromising rest, focus, or patience? Name a truer response you can practice.
Where did order break down in the last seven days? Trace the pattern through mind, body, or soul and choose one rhythm to revisit.

title: The Creative Framework
prompts: What work would you create if your attention were protected? What would you stop consuming or doing to give it room?
What single craft are you deepening? What evidence or small experiment would help you practice it systematically while honoring your other responsibilities?
Name a turning point in your craft and who stood with you. What story or example from the saints helps you understand that change?
What costly lesson has your craft taught you about discipline or vocation? What passage helps you examine it?
What observable fruit would show that practice is serving its purpose? Describe a finish line that leaves room for real rest.
What objection or shortcut needs a truthful answer? Which skill must you build through practice before you claim it?
What is the first sign that the work has drifted from its purpose? Identify a principle and a recurring practice that would address it.

title: The Psychological Framework
prompts: What would peace and relational order look like if those closest to you received your best attention and care?
Where is your personal discipline helping the people closest to you? Where could remembering their dignity change how you show up?
What experience can you communicate in service of others, and what blind spot should you keep in view when telling it?
Where are you swinging between extremes with someone close to you? What do you sense, what remains uncertain, and how do you intend to respond?
If you kept showing up faithfully for five years, what would have changed for the people or community you serve?
Name a reactive pattern you want to leave behind and the boundary or commitment you want to practice in its place.
What relational pattern keeps returning, and where do you notice it first? What rhythm of care, accountability, or support would help you respond?
